build.reason: The supplied recipe compiles and links the xinclude target, but the supplied evidence does not establish the effective feature defaults or a successful build.

input.reason: A finite input can provide zero allocation-failure limit, a main URL and well-formed XML with an xi:include carrying an invalid parse value; the entry passes that document to XInclude processing.

lifecycle.reason: For a successfully parsed document and allocated XInclude context, the OLD entry processes the node while the context is live and then frees the context and document.

control_flow.reason: The entry calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode on the parsed document; processing traverses to xi:include, expands it, reads its parse attribute and can raise an XInclude error. The context callback is consulted at that error site.

accepted.requirement: The XInclude-context operation must be able to deliver XInclude and delegated parser or XPointer errors to a context-local structured callback with its supplied data.
accepted.target_route: The OLD entry reads a main XML entity, parses it, creates an xmlXIncludeCtxt, sets flags and calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode. A finite well-formed document containing xi:include with an invalid parse value reaches xmlXIncludeErr. The changed setter can install the structured callback on that same context, and included-document parsing and XPointer evaluation conditionally forward it.
accepted.failure_condition: The OLD entry never calls xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler. xmlXIncludeNewContext zero-initializes errorHandler and errorCtxt, leaving the context-local structured route unreachable for every input.
accepted.alternative_paths: Input bytes only determine options and entities, not the private callback fields. The initializer installs a generic variadic error function, whose signature and registration differ from a context-local structured callback. The included-parser and XPointer forwarding paths both require the same non-NULL context callback, so they provide no equivalent route.
